Every interactive app on this site can be dropped into another web page --
lecture notes, a course site, a blog post -- as an `<iframe>`. Add `embed=1`
to the app's URL and the page renders the app alone -- its controls and its
chart, with none of the page's explanation, none of the diagnostic plots and
tables under the chart, and no navigation bar, sidebar, title or footer.

```html
<iframe
  src="https://www.visualmathlab.com/apps/newton-method/?embed=1&f=x^3-2&x0=1"
  width="100%" height="720" loading="lazy"
  title="Newton's method">
</iframe>
```

## Choosing what the app opens with

Every input on an app page is mirrored in its URL, so the parameters you see
in the address bar after setting up an app are the parameters to put in the
`src`. Set the function, endpoints, step counts and options the way you want
readers to first see them, copy the URL, and append `&embed=1`. Readers can
still change everything once the app has loaded; the URL only sets the
starting point.

## Pages with more than one app

A few pages hold several interactive figures, one per step of an argument.
`embed=1` gives the first; to frame a later one, name it instead of `1`.
[Sperner's Lemma -- Combinatorial Proof](apps/sperners-lemma-combinatorial-proof/index.qmd)
has three: `embed=triangulation` (the colored triangulation at the top, the
same as `embed=1`), `embed=doors` (the three kinds of room) and
`embed=boundary` (the bottom edge on its own). A name no figure on the page
carries falls back to the first.

```html
<iframe
  src="https://www.visualmathlab.com/apps/sperners-lemma-combinatorial-proof/?embed=boundary"
  width="100%" height="480" loading="lazy"
  title="Sperner's lemma on the bottom edge">
</iframe>
```

## Size

An app's chart is sized to the frame it is given, so pick a `height` that
suits the page around it -- `720` pixels leaves room for the controls panel
and a comfortable chart on a laptop screen; `900` if the app has a long
controls panel. Nothing below the chart is shown, so the frame never needs
to be taller than the controls and the chart together. `width="100%"` lets the frame follow your column. Below about
600 pixels of width the controls stack vertically, which works but is
cramped; on a narrow layout consider linking to the app instead.

## Privacy

An embedded app sets no cookies, shows no analytics banner, and records
nothing: analytics never run in embed mode, even for a visitor who allowed
them on a direct visit to this site. Everything else in the
[privacy policy](privacy.qmd) applies -- in particular, the app still loads
Plotly and math.js from their public CDNs.

## Building your own

The chart theming, control panels, sliders and numerical helpers these apps
are built from are a separate open-source library,
[mathviz](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz), packaged as a Quarto
extension (`quarto add apurvanakade/mathviz`) and as a plain script bundle
for any other site. If you would rather write an app of your own in the same
style than embed one of these, start there.
